source.title: Emergence of Minimal Circuits for Indirect Object Identification in Attention-Only Transformers

page_placements.theme: Constructed IOI models expose architectural requirements

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests IOI circuits in task-trained attention-only models and finds a compact mechanism unlike the multi-hop GPT-2 small circuit, refining the scope of claims about circuit generality. It does not reproduce the GPT-2 small analysis.
record.gate_note: The study reports symbolic-task accuracy, attention patterns, residual-stream decomposition, and composition ablations. The discussion of GPT-2 small is background, not a new result. Eigenvalue details are not separately recorded because they do not directly test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains attention-only toy transformers from scratch on a symbolic IOI task and reverse-engineers their mechanism. This is a new setting with a result on V3: whether the same head classes and roles carry IOI in other models. The one-layer two-head model uses an additive/contrastive two-head solution rather than GPT-2 small's duplicate-token, S-inhibition and name-mover classes. It never studies the GPT-2 small circuit itself, so V1, V2, V4, V5 and V6 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a one-layer, one-head model fails, while a one-layer, two-head attention-only model solves symbolic IOI perfectly via additive and contrastive heads. A two-layer, one-head model composes across layers. Task-constrained training yields simpler circuits than broadly pretrained models. Note that the abstract says the composition is 'primarily through query-key interactions', but Section 4.3.3 reports heavy reliance on both Q- and V-composition, with K-composition mattering least.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains small attention-only models from scratch on a symbolic IOI task and analyzes their attention, residual streams, and composition. It does not apply the GPT-2 small circuit-discovery and faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy differs with positional embeddings: the model reaches 100% with them and ≈70% without them. In the two-layer model, Q-, V-, and K-composition ablations have different reported effects.

fits_no_version.finding: A one-layer, one-head attention-only model cannot solve symbolic IOI, while two heads with the same parameter count solve it perfectly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimal architectural requirements for IOI: at least two attention heads (or two layers) are needed in attention-only models.

fits_no_version.finding: Without positional embeddings the two-head model reaches ≈70% accuracy, and its heads show similar attention patterns rather than distinct roles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In toy IOI models, head specialization depends on the availability of positional information.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The task uses rigid six-token symbolic sequences rather than natural-language prompts. The authors state that varying sequence lengths, multiple interdependent clauses, dynamic syntax, and training dynamics are not studied. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported performance results.
record.rows_left_out: Spectral eigenvalue descriptions in Sections 4.2.3 and Figures 5–6 were left out because they do not directly test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: GPT-2 small, the 26-head 7-class circuit, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not examined.
No name-mover ablation and no backup-head test.
Other pretrained models, sizes and training checkpoints are not tested. Component reuse on other tasks is not tested. The two-layer model's heads are not mapped to GPT-2 classes.
No comparison of circuit-discovery methods, ablation types or metrics.
Circuit faithfulness and completeness are not evaluated under different ablations, metrics or distributions.
The GPT-2 circuit is not tested across name orders, templates or more names. The toy model's two templates are its training set.

missing.what: Two-layer model attention patterns: the first layer's S2 token aggregates name information that the second layer reads. This is a multi-hop structure partly resembling GPT-2's, and bears on V3 for the two-layer model.

Averaged-name-embedding analysis of the positional embeddings model: the first head is positional, and the second integrates positional and contextual cues. This bears on how the head roles differ from GPT-2 classes.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T3: this is a new setting with a mechanistic result, not a direct argument against the GPT-2 circuit. V6 links were removed from all rows because the toy circuit is not the GPT-2 circuit, and the two templates are the training data rather than a test of prompt variants. The record's V6 labels are therefore dropped. The record's V3 'challenges' label is softened to 'limits_scope' for two reasons. First, V3 most plausibly concerns pretrained models, and this is a task-only toy model. Second, the two-layer model's Q/V composition is not mapped to GPT-2 head classes, so rows r9–r11 cannot decide the question. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the results are for single training runs.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test GPT-2 small, the 26-head seven-class circuit, or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
No ablation of main name-mover heads or test of backup heads taking over.
No other pretrained model sizes or checkpoints are tested, and component reuse on other tasks is not examined.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics for recovering the same circuit.
The study does not compare faithfulness or completeness under different circuit ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions.
The study tests two rigid symbolic templates and a six-name vocabulary, but not natural-language prompt formats, sequences containing more than two distinct names, or more complex syntax.

rows.subject: zero-layer model
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on the symbolic IOI task as a bigram model.
rows.measure: accuracy / probability assigned to the correct name
rows.note: The authors attribute the result to lack of prior-context use.
rows.check: This is a capacity baseline (a zero-layer bigram gets 16.7%). It says nothing about which head classes carry IOI, so it does not bear on V3.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1: equal probability of approximately 16.7% per name.

rows.subject: single-layer, single-head model
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, one head; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on the symbolic IOI task.
rows.measure: ability to distinguish and predict the correct name
rows.value: Assigns ≈0.5 probability for the names in the prompt but cannot distinguish which is correct.
rows.note: The paper says the single head cannot jointly perform reference detection and copying.
rows.check: This is a capacity baseline: a single head cannot solve the task. It shows nothing about circuit classes or roles.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1 and Figure 1: approximately 0.5 probability per candidate name without distinguishing the correct one.

rows.subject: two-heads, one-layer model
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, two heads; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on the complete symbolic IOI dataset.
rows.note: The dataset uses two distinct names per sequence and two fixed templates.
rows.check: Accuracy alone cannot show whether the same circuit is used. V6 concerns the GPT-2 circuit across prompt variants, but the toy model's circuit is not that circuit, and two fixed symbolic templates are training data, not a variant test.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2 opening paragraph: perfect accuracy; Sections 3.1–3.2.1: six names, two templates and all 60 sequences.

rows.subject: two-heads, one-layer model
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, two heads; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Measured average attention patterns across possible inputs.
rows.measure: head attention targets and inferred roles
rows.value: The first head attends to the two names in the dependent clause; the second attends to the main-clause subject and the non-repeated dependent-clause name.
rows.note: The accompanying text describes these patterns and says the second head's pattern depends on the template.
rows.check: In the one-layer model, the head roles are 'attend to both names' and 'attend to S2 plus the non-repeated name'. The paper sets these against GPT-2's multi-hop classes, so the same classes are absent. V6 was removed from this row because this is not the GPT-2 circuit.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2.1 and Figures 2–3: first head attends to both initial names; second attends to the main-clause subject and the non-repeated name.

rows.subject: two-heads, one-layer model
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, two heads; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Decomposed residual-stream contributions and projected them onto name directions.
rows.measure: alignment of head output with correct/incorrect-name sum and difference directions
rows.value: The first head's output aligns closest with the sum direction (correct + incorrect).
rows.note: The text describes the result and characterizes this head as aggregating signals additively.
rows.check: The additive (sum-direction) head role is not one of GPT-2 small's head classes. The value comes from a figure only.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2.2 and Figure 4: first head aligns most closely with the correct-plus-incorrect direction.

rows.subject: two-heads, one-layer model
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, two heads; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Decomposed residual-stream contributions and projected them onto name directions.
rows.measure: alignment of head output with correct/incorrect-name sum and difference directions
rows.value: The second head's output aligns closest with the difference direction (correct − incorrect).
rows.note: The text describes this as contrastive suppression, while noting the head also has a component in the correct-token direction.
rows.check: The contrastive (difference-direction) head computes the answer in a single layer, with no separate S-inhibition to name-mover hop. The value comes from a figure only.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2.2 and Figure 4: second head aligns most closely with the correct-minus-incorrect direction, with additional components.

rows.subject: two-heads, one-layer model without positional embeddings
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, two heads; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch without positional embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Trained the same architecture without positional embeddings.
rows.baseline: 100% for the model with positional embeddings
rows.note: The authors report ≈67% probability on the correct token and say positional embeddings are not strictly necessary, while they enable 100% accuracy.
rows.check: This is an ablation of the toy model's own architecture (no positional embeddings). It does not bear on whether the GPT-2 circuit classes recur, and it is not a prompt-variant test, so V6 does not apply.

rows.subject: two-heads, one-layer model without positional embeddings
rows.size_stated: one attention layer, two heads; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch without positional embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Measured average attention patterns after assigning all name tokens a single averaged embedding.
rows.value: The two heads show similar attention patterns and focus primarily on the correct non-repeated name.
rows.note: The text describes the patterns but does not quantify them.
rows.check: This row reports the attention pattern of the variant without positional embeddings. The figure is described as from a model trained without positional embeddings, not one with averaged embeddings, so the condition label 'averaged name embeddings' is likely conflated with Section 4.2.4. The row does not map to GPT-2 classes.

rows.subject: two-layer, one-head model
rows.size_stated: two attention layers, one head per layer; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Ablated Q-composition by subtracting the first-layer output from the corresponding input to the Q matrix.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as strong reliance on Q-composition.
rows.check: Q-composition reliance (≈100% drop) shows that a cross-layer hierarchy exists. The heads are never mapped to duplicate-token, S-inhibition or name-mover roles, so it cannot show whether the classes match.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3.3: removing Q-composition produces an approximately 100% accuracy drop.

rows.subject: two-layer, one-head model
rows.size_stated: two attention layers, one head per layer; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Ablated V-composition by subtracting the first-layer output from the corresponding input to the V matrix.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as strong reliance on V-composition.
rows.check: V-composition reliance (≈93.33% drop) is likewise not mapped to GPT-2 head classes.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3.3: removing V-composition produces an approximately 93.33% accuracy drop.

rows.subject: two-layer, one-head model
rows.size_stated: two attention layers, one head per layer; residual stream dimension 8
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on symbolic IOI
rows.operation_detail: Ablated K-composition by subtracting the first-layer output from the corresponding input to the K matrix.
rows.note: The authors report a smaller effect than for Q- and V-composition.
rows.check: The K-composition ablation (≈26.67% drop) is not mapped to GPT-2 head classes, and the record's 'partial' state has no reference version effect to compare against.

relationships.condition: One-layer, two-head attention-only model trained from scratch on symbolic IOI (6 names, BABA/BAAB)
relationships.reason: IOI is solved perfectly by an additive head plus a contrastive head, not GPT-2's multi-hop duplicate-token, S-inhibition and name-mover classes (r4, r5, r6). The same classes do not emerge in task-only toy training.
relationships.display_finding: A one-layer, two-head model achieves perfect symbolic IOI performance using additive and contrastive heads instead of the multi-hop duplicate-token, S-inhibition and name-mover classes.

labels.reason: Rows r4–r6 identify a direct additive–contrastive solution rather than GPT-2's multi-hop circuit. This qualifies circuit transfer in the restricted task-trained setting; reuse on other tasks remains untested.

relation.reason: The study analyzes its own trained models and identifies an alternative IOI mechanism, providing evidence about V3.

tranche.reason: From-scratch symbolic IOI training is a new setting; the recovered additive–contrastive mechanism bears on V3's proposed transfer of circuit classes.

source_check.notes: All 60 possible sequences appear in every training batch; perfect accuracy does not establish held-out generalization. The abstract emphasizes query-key interactions, but Section 4.3.3 reports strongest dependence on Q- and V-composition.

reader_labels.reason: The two-head model uses an additive/contrastive division of labor, and the two-layer model relies on cross-layer Q- and V-composition; these are not the claimed GPT-2 small head classes and circuit. See r4–r6 and r9–r11.
